body: Rotations also invalidate the shadow map cache. So, the current workaround in my game "wiggles" the `Sprite3D` by rotating on the local Y-axis by `0.000_001` radians while the camera is moving.

Seeing `renderer_scene_cull.cpp`, I see that animated materials trigger the shadow cache dirty flag in `RendererSceneCull::_light_instance_update_shadow`.
I think either a fix could be made by 1. having shadow dirty flag triggering in dedicated update trigger for camera movement - there doesn't seem to be one that affects the scene culling / shadow dirty flag triggering that calls `make_shadow_dirty()` at the moment,
or 2. adding usage of view dependent billboards as to be handled like animated materials. 
The second seems like an easier and simpler fix for me, but I'm not sure how Godot contributors feel about the implicitness of billboards being considered "animated". 
Also this would add the overhead of billboards always invalidating shadow cache even if the camera does not move in a significant manner, which I could see losing a lot of performance with scenes with fixed view orthographic cameras with a lot of Spirte3D's. (Such as platformers or side scroller games.)
So I guess the better fix in performance would be number 1, but I'm not sure it is worth editing some important function such as `RendererSceneCull::_render_scene`, especially as a no-time contributor to Godot.
Does anyone have thoughts on the fix approach to this matter?
